prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B011 as a single part with Buchwald and Hartwig. After the full first round it is the only candidate on which the objections are about classification and not about evidence: no member disputes the science, the mechanism (oxidative addition, amine binding, base-assisted deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination) is established by isolated intermediates and kinetics, and the ligand-design logic explains why the reaction went from a curiosity to a predictable method. Three decades of independent use in medicinal and process chemistry give a verification record that none of the biology-facing candidates can yet match. Attribution is also the cleanest on the list: two people, working independently from the mid-1990s, made the reaction general, and nobody has argued that a third name is needed. The citation should say 'general' and 'ligand-controlled' so that what is honoured is the generality, not the bond type.
statement.case_against: The strongest argument against is the 2010 prize for palladium cross-coupling. I do not think C-N coupling is a second helping of the same achievement, but I accept that a committee could read it as the same toolbox applied to a new bond, and then B011 has no advantage over candidates that open a new field. A second weakness is that a single-part prize in a year when the shortlist is dominated by biology-facing work may look conservative. Finally, leaving out Kosugi means a documented precursor is not named in the citation; I think that is right, but it will draw comment.

responses.point: C-N bond formation needed its own mechanistic and ligand solutions, so it is not a continuation of the 2010 C-C coupling prize, and Kosugi's tin-amide work should not take a place.
responses.response: I agree, and I will answer the chair's question from the structural side. What the 1994-1995 work supplied that the 1983 tin-amide reaction lacked was a catalytic system that used free amines with a base, instead of stoichiometric toxic aminostannanes, and a ligand framework (bulky, electron-rich phosphines, later chelating and biaryl types) that made reductive elimination of the C-N bond competitive with beta-hydride elimination. That is what widened the scope to primary amines and functional-group-rich substrates. Peter, I would still ask you to confirm the priority dates for Kosugi and Migita, because I would like the committee's background text to state them accurately and not by assertion.

responses.point: A two-part prize pairing a clean synthetic-methods part (B011) with a chemical-biology part (B008, Liu alone) gives a coherent prize explainable in a sentence each, within three people.
responses.response: I considered this seriously and have not moved. My objection is not to base editing as science but to the pairing logic: one part is a three-decade-old method with a settled record and the other is a field whose clinical and off-target record is still short, as you note yourself. Combining them does not strengthen B011 and makes the weaker part carry the risk for the whole prize. I also think Liu alone is hard to defend against Komor and Gaudelli, and Chabes and Aqvist have both raised the Nishida and Kondo work, so a clean second part would need more agreement than the committee currently has. If the committee settles on a two-part prize, I would accept B008 as the second part, but I would prefer to see that choice made on its own merits and not as a means of balancing subfields.

responses.point: Base editing is a distinct chemical idea, direct nucleotide conversion without a break, and Komor and Gaudelli made distinct cytosine and adenine editors, so a Liu-only prize hides their contribution.
responses.response: Your mechanistic argument persuades me more than it did in round 1, and I have kept B008 as my first alternative. What stops me from preferring it is how little structural evidence the committee has so far seen for the editing outcome itself: bystander deamination and sequence-context effects are still being characterised, and the adenine deaminase was evolved, not designed, so the mechanism of its action on DNA is less well understood than the C-N cycle. I would reconsider if the expert reports show that bystander and off-target behaviour is now well controlled in patients, not only in cell culture.

responses.point: B011 is a major extension of an already awarded concept, whereas B009 opens a new modality; B011 is nevertheless the least contested on maturity and attribution.
responses.response: I accept the distinction between extending a concept and opening a modality, and I think it is the right way to frame the 2010 overlap. My answer is that a prize does not have to open a new field if it recognises a different transformation whose chemistry had to be solved separately, and C-N coupling is that. On B009 I agree with your own qualifier that the field is promising, not yet validated by an approved degrader, and the credit among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ito, Ciulli and Gray cannot yet be cut to three without losing a strand. If you are willing to say you would not stand in the way of B011, I would take that as a good sign for a prize this year, and I would be glad to see B009 return when the clinical record is clearer.

responses.point: Lipid nanoparticles open a field no prize has recognised, and the 2023 Medicine prize addressed the cargo and not the delivery chemistry; B011 is a safe consensus fallback.
responses.response: I accept that the 2023 prize addressed the cargo and that the clinical validation of B016 is the strongest on the list. I also note that the narrower definition you and Sparr describe (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids and encapsulation) is a useful one. The problem remains the trio: you now credit Cullis, Hope and Anderson, Sparr credits Cullis, Hope and Madden, and both of you tell us that MacLachlan, Madden or Langer have real claims. A prize that two of its proponents cannot agree on at the level of names is not yet ready for a vote. I would rather the committee treat B011 as a prize it can defend today than as a fallback. If the committee does settle the names, I would want the citation to be narrow and about the ionizable-lipid design principle.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or reads it as the same toolbox on a new bond.
Exact priority dates for Kosugi and Migita relative to the first Pd-catalysed amine systems, which Somfai has not yet confirmed.
Whether a single-part prize is the right shape when five of the shortlisted fields are biology-facing, and whether the committee will want a second part.
Whether the base-editing record (bystander and off-target behaviour, Nishida and Kondo priority) will be settled enough in the expert reports to move B008 above B011.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B011, B008 or B043. Peter Brzezinski is a Stockholm University colleague, but no shortlisted candidate is connected to my institution or to my own work. My electron crystallography and porous-materials background is relevant to B043 only as expertise, not as a tie to any named candidate.
